description: Migrates all data models from the source environment to the target environment in batches.

dependencies.description: Dependencies to include in the migration. If None or "all", all supported dependencies are included by default. Supported values: - "dataSecurity" (includes both Data Security and Scope Configuration) - "formulas" (for Formulas) - "hierarchies" (for Drill Hierarchies) - "perspectives" (for Perspectives)

shares.description: Whether to also migrate data model shares after the schema import.

batch_size.description: Number of data models to migrate per batch.

sleep_time.description: Time (in seconds) to sleep between batches.

action.description: Strategy to handle existing data models in the target environment. - "overwrite": Attempts to overwrite an existing model using its original ID via the ``datamodelId`` parameter. If the model is not found in the target environment, it falls back to creating the model. - "duplicate": Creates a new model by appending " (Duplicate)" to the original name.

emit.description: Optional callback invoked with structured progress events. If not provided, the method emits no events and only returns a final result. Event payloads follow a consistent shape: - ``type``: str ("started" | "progress" | "warning" | "error" | "completed") - ``step``: str logical step identifier - ``message``: str human-readable message - Additional fields depending on the step (counts, status_code, etc.)

examples.user_query: How can I migrate all data models, including data security and formulas, to a new environment while overwriting existing models?
examples.notes: This call migrates all data models with data security and formulas dependencies included. Existing models in the target environment will be overwritten if they already exist.

examples.user_query: I want to migrate all data models with all dependencies and duplicate any existing models in the target environment. How can I do this?
examples.notes: This call migrates all data models with all dependencies and includes data model shares. Existing models in the target environment will not be overwritten but duplicated with a new name.

examples.user_query: Can I migrate data models in small batches with a custom progress callback to track the migration process?
examples.notes: This call migrates data models with hierarchies and perspectives dependencies in small batches of 5, including data model shares. A custom callback is used to track the migration progress.

description: Migrates specific data models from the source environment to the target environment.

datamodel_ids.description: A list of data model IDs to migrate. Either `datamodel_ids` or `datamodel_names` must be provided.

datamodel_names.description: A list of data model names to migrate. Either `datamodel_ids` or `datamodel_names` must be provided.

provider_connection_map.description: A dictionary mapping provider names to connection IDs. This allows specifying different connections per provider. Example: { "Databricks": "Connection ID", "GoogleBigQuery": "Connection ID" }

dependencies.description: A list of dependencies to include in the migration. If not provided or if "all" is passed, all dependencies are selected by default. Possible values: - "dataSecurity" (includes both Data Security and Scope Configuration) - "formulas" (for Formulas) - "hierarchies" (for Drill Hierarchies) - "perspectives" (for Perspectives) If left blank or set to "all", all dependencies are included by default.

shares.description: Whether to also migrate the data model's shares.

action.description: Strategy to handle existing data models in the target environment. - "overwrite": Attempts to overwrite existing model using its original ID via the datamodelId parameter. If the model is not found in target environment, it will automatically fall back and create the model. - "duplicate": Creates a new model by passing a `new_title` to the `newTitle` parameter of the import API. If `new_title` is not provided, the original title will be used with " (Duplicate)" appended.

new_title.description: New name for the duplicated data model. Used only when `action='duplicate'`.

emit.description: Optional callback invoked with structured progress events. If not provided, the method emits no events and only returns a final result. Event payloads follow a consistent shape: - ``type``: str ("started" | "progress" | "warning" | "error" | "completed") - ``step``: str logical step identifier - ``message``: str human-readable message - Additional fields depending on the step (counts, status_code, etc.)

examples.user_query: How can I migrate the data models with IDs 'dm_123' and 'dm_456' to the target environment, including all dependencies and shares?
examples.notes: This call migrates two specific data models by their IDs, including all dependencies and shares, and overwrites any existing models in the target environment.

examples.user_query: I want to migrate data models named 'SalesModel' and 'MarketingModel' to the target environment, but I want to duplicate them with new names.
examples.notes: This call migrates two data models by their names and creates duplicates in the target environment with a new title.

examples.user_query: Can I migrate the 'FinanceModel' data model using a specific connection for Databricks and include only formulas and hierarchies?
examples.notes: This call migrates the 'FinanceModel' data model using a specific connection for Databricks, includes only formulas and hierarchies as dependencies, and does not migrate shares.
